results.content: April 29, 2026 Call for Papers: Eastern European Holocaust Studies: Jewish Religious Life during the Holocaust. The editors of the journal Eastern European Holocaust Studies: Jewish Religious Life during the Holocaust invite submissions that examine Jewish religious life during the Holocaust and in its immediate aftermath. Contributions may explore how Jews sought to maintain, adapt to, or struggle with religious practice under Nazi persecution, including prayer and liturgy, the observance of Shabbat and Jewish holidays, life-cycle rituals (brit milah, marriage, and burial), rabbinic authority and leadership, clandestine worship, the smuggling of religious objects, theological and philosophical responses to suffering and divine absence, and the role of religion in the everyday life of refugees, as well as of Jewish men, women, and children in ghettos, camps, and in hiding. The European Association for Jewish Studies (EAJS) invites members of the EAJS and participants of the CEU conference ‘Jewish Studies at the Crossroads’ to join a Nahmanides-Forum on the impact of the events of and after 7 October 2023 on Jewish Studies taking place at the CEU Vienna June 3, 2026.

Alongside established artists, emerging artists at the beginning of their journey in naive and primitive art are also supported. His works are held in private collections in Russia as well as in England, the Netherlands, Latvia, Kazakhstan, Italy, Germany, Bahrain, Australia, and the USA, and also in the All-Russian Historical and Ethnographic Museum. “The work is dedicated to remembering and forgetting, appearing, and disappearing,” Karolina Żyniewicz notes about *Sign of the Times*, “resisting the passage of time, and confronting the imperfections of human memory.” During the exhibition opening hours (Thu – Sun, 2 – 6 pm) at Art Laboratory Berlin, Żyniewicz will perform her transcription from Thursdays to Saturdays, while being present Sundays to talk to visitors, and if they wish, lead further interviews that may contribute to future iterations of this research project.
